entityName: Athena Research and Innovation Center in Information, Communication and Knowledge Technologies
description:
Athena Research Centre was founded in 2003 as the “IRIS – Integrated Research for the Information Society” to consolidate and further expand the Greek R&D activities and initiatives in the area of ICT. The new Center initially comprised of the following existing institutes: the Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP), the Cultural and Educational Technology Institute (CETI) and the Industrial Systems Institute (ISI). The founding act provided for the creation of new institutes that would cover vibrant areas of digital technology as well as of units that would incubate knowhow development activities that may lead to new major development directions. In 2006 IRIS was renamed to “Research and Innovation Center in Information, Communication and Knowledge Technologies”, with the name designation “Athena”.

The vision of Athena is to serve the full spectrum of the research lifecycle, starting from basic and applied research, continuing on to system & product building and infrastructure service provision, and ending with technology transfer and entrepreneurship. The fundamental role of Athena is to build knowledge and devise solutions and technologies for the digital society. Its value lies in the unique collection of skills and know-how of its researchers and professional staff and its national and international reputation.

The overall strategy and research values of Athena are developing along these axes: a) A research plan that targets fundamental and applied challenges with high potential impact, aiming at high-quality, novel, and deep results, with informatics at the core of synergies with other sciences, b) A technology transfer plan with a global focus and special attention to the Greek environment, c) A young researcher development plan based on identifying and supporting original talent, d) A strategic co-operations plan aiming at key industrial companies, governmental agencies, regional authorities, and international research and higher-education organisations, e) An educational plan that targets at designing and participating in local and international graduate programs.

Athena is organised today in the following Institutes and Units: a) Information Management Systems Institute (Maroussi), b) Institute of Language and Speech Processing (Maroussi), c) Industrial Systems Institute (Patras), d) Corallia (Maroussi), e) Space Programmes Unit (Maroussi), f) Robotics Perception and Interaction Unit (Maroussi), g) Environmental and Networking Technologies and Applications Unit (Xanthi), h) Pharma Informatics Unit (Maroussi).

Athena has premises and infrastructures in three geographical regions of Greece: Attica - Athens, Western Greece - Patras and Thrace - Xanthi. The Central Administration is located in Athens. This gives Athena a wider, country-wide role and offers unique advantages: a) closer and stronger connections to the regional, academic and industrial environment, b) employee engagement in regional resources and activities, c) enhancing regional competitiveness by providing immediate access to the innovation created, d) taking advantage of the initiatives, funding schemes and other opportunities provided exclusively to regions.

entityDescription:
Planetek Italia s.r.l. is an Italian Benefit Company established in 1994, headquartered in Bari, part of D-Orbit Group since 2025.
Planetek Italia s.r.l. is a leading Italian company specializing in geospatial data solutions, with a presence in both national and international markets. 
The company owns Planetek Hellas EPE, located in Athens, Greece, and two Italian university spin-offs: GAP s.r.l. and GEO-K s.r.l.

Planetek Italia delivers comprehensive solutions for harnessing the value of geospatial data across the entire data life cycle—ranging from acquisition and storage to management, analysis, and dissemination. 
The company operates in a wide array of application domains, including environmental and land monitoring, open government, smart cities, defense and security, space exploration, and Earth Observation (EO) satellite missions.With extensive expertise in Earth Observation technologies, Planetek develops solutions that utilize optical and radar data from satellites, aircraft, and drones. Its innovations include software for both on-board edge computing and ground segment operations, along with geo-analytics products and value-added services for environmental monitoring.
The company integrates artificial intelligence into its remote sensing data processing workflows and provides EO-based services—such as geo-analytics, dynamic visualizations, and automated reporting—through its proprietary Rheticus® cloud-based platform.

Planetek Italia employs over 130 professionals and reported a financial turnover of approximately €18 million in 2023.

In November 2022, Planetek was among the first 22 European space companies to sign the “Statement for a Responsible Space Sector” initiative promoted by the European Space Agency (ESA). This commitment supports the sustainable development of the space sector and promotes the positive impact of space activities on society.The company adheres to the principles of SDesign Thinking to ensure the development of user-centric solutions, leveraging the best available technologies while maintaining a strong commitment to economic, social, and environmental sustainability.In 2022, Planetek Italia became a member of Assobenefit, the Italian Association of Benefit Corporations, and released its first Sustainability Report, which demonstrated outstanding performance, ranking among the highest in the ICT and Aerospace sectors. In 2023, the company was recognized with the Sustainability Hero award for Italy under the SME EnterPRIZE initiative, a European program that highlights businesses with sustainability-driven models.

Planetek Italia operates under a structured model based on Corporate Functions and Strategic Business Units (SBUs). Each SBU functions with a high degree of autonomy and includes dedicated teams for design, sales, and production.

The company also maintains rigorous quality and compliance standards:It operates an Information Security Management System certified under ISO/IEC 27001:2013.It is certified for remote sensing services in line with the ISO 9001 standard.It applies an Environmental Management System compliant with ISO 14001:2015 and EU Regulation No. 1221/2009 (EMAS III).It holds SA8000 certification for social accountability, which includes a strong commitment to gender equality and ethical labor practices.

The company started in the field of servicing cutting tools in 1998.
After the very beginnings, MASAM s.r.o. was founded in 2001. Its primary focus was servicing cutting tools. In a short period requirements and customer expectations increased, and consequently it was necessary to reconsider the focus and plans for the future in terms of investment and development of the company.
Between the years 2001 and 2006 the company invested in development through the purchase of new CNC technologies, which allowed us to provide not only services but also the production of cutting tools. This has resulted in the expansion of our production. We supplemented technology, construction, entry and exit checks. For full qualitatively managed processes in the company, during this period we introduced an information management system and certification according to ISO 9001:2008. In 2006, the entire company moved into the newly built premises.
Since 2006 the company has experienced the next period of development and expansion. First there was just an idea of expanding the company with the chip machining and tool room. We were able to test the cutting tools we produced and, of course, also use them for our chip machining needs. During the years 2006 – 2009 it was decided to extend MASAM s.r.o. by two divisions: The Manufacture and Sharpening of Cutting Tools Division and the Chip Machining, Tool Room Division. We started expanding our commercial department, aimed at discovering new markets and new customers for both divisions.
In 2013, the new manufacturing plant in the Vráble industrial park was completed. It is a modern hall, which offers the perfect base for further development. Our goal is to have the most modern machinery permitting us to meet the most demanding requirements of our customers.

The application of light metals provides a huge weight reduction potential, which in turn has a positive effect on the energy efficiency and CO2 emissions of vehicles.

Striving to rise to these challenges, the LKR team of more than 50 specialists has both cutting-edge simulation tools as well as a unique research infrastructure at its disposal. This allows new metal alloys and customized processes for casting of lightweight components and metal forming to be developed and prototyped.

entityDescription:
Scientific and teaching activities as well as collaboration with industry in the area of aerospace dynamics, mechatronical systems and space robotics is conducted at the Chair of Flight Vehicle Dynamics, and related Laboratory for Flight Vehicle Dynamics and Multibody Systems. To this end, special research focus of the Chair and Laboratory is on the mathematical and numerical modelling of multibody/multi-physical systems, computational dynamics as well as flight mechanics and control, including advanced machine/deep learning algorithms and data-driven surrogate models. CoNISMa entered in the EU Marine Board, being a unique super-organism in Europe, since it merges scientific and capacity building activities. Through CoNISMa, the Italian University-based research and capacity building system working on marine sciences became a single entity and reached international size and reputation as such. CoNISMa covers all fields of marine sciences, with both research and capacity building activities ranging from physics to chemistry, geology, biology, ecology, engineering, economics, and legal sciences. It carries out its activities worldwide. The administrative offices are located in Rome, but the bulk of the "staff" and "infrastructures" is in the associated Universities.

entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE OF AERODYNAMICS AND FLOW TECHNOLOGY (DLR AS)
entityDescription:
The Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology is a leading research Institute in the field of aerodynamics/aeroacoustics of airplanes and aerothermodynamics of space vehicles. It has two main sites at Braunschweig and Göttingen and a division at Cologne. Today a total personal of about 350 employees is engaged in numerical and experimental investigations on air- and space vehicles. Experiments are performed in wind tunnels and in flight experimental aircraft.
The Institute can look back on a long history: After the first “Modellversuchsanstalt für Aerodynamik“ was founded in Göttingen in 1907, the Institute for Aerodynamics and the Institute for Gas Dynamics of the "Deutsche Forschungsanstalt für Luftfahrt” (DFL) were succeeded by today's DLR Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology.
As a leading research institute in the fields of aerodynamics, aeroacoustics and aerothermodynamics, it is subdivided into nine departments. The Institute is acting as a link between basic research at the universities and industrial application. This results in a large number of cooperative national and international research projects.
Environmental policy conditions are playing an increasingly major role in air traffic. The DLR Institute of Aerodynamics and Flow Technology therefore researches how future aircraft and space transportation systems can be designed and operated more efficient, ecological, comfortable, economical and secure. A further core competence is the development of software products used for aerodynamic and aeroacoustic simulations.
